verdict.applicable_scope: fixed synthetic F0/F1 T1 slice, closed-world enumeration; not open-language ability, not whole-model acceptance
verdict.correction_note: first draft of this field said the query answers collapse; the per-arm decomposition disproved it before publication — parser_permuted keeps query 0.984. The corrected reading is above.
verdict.credit_boundary: answer loss reaches V4 only; producer prediction is detached before state commit, so answer-error credit to the producer is NOT established by this pack
verdict.mechanism_that_carries_the_gain: writing the post-correction world state: disabling writes collapses f1_state_query from ~0.995 to ~0.379 on the same checkpoints, and zeroes post_correction_state_exact and unrelated_keep_exact
verdict.non_responsible_updates: responsible_owner_frozen ≈ 0.387 ⇒ updates outside the frozen responsible receiver produce about a third of the gain
verdict.parser_label_dependence: parser_permuted keeps ~0.49 of the score ⇒ roughly half the gain depends on correct parser structure labels
verdict.readout_side_updates_alone: readout_only ≈ no_update (0.010 vs 0.000) ⇒ turning only the readout does not produce the behaviour
verdict.which_half_collapses: the state-write half, not the answer half. correct: state 1.000 / query 0.990 / correction-answer 0.995 / unrelated-keep 1.000. parser_permuted: state 0.000 / unrelated-keep 0.000 BUT query 0.984 and correction-answer 0.992 ⇒ it still answers correctly while never writing the correct world state. responsible_owner_frozen: state 0.000 / query 0.773 / answer 0.977. So answer text is not the discriminator; post-correction world state (and the unrelated-fact hold) is.
